title: For the last 6 months I’ve been building AutoSprite, a tool that turns one character image into full animated spritesheets
author: beelllllll
selftext:
I’ve been building AutoSprite for the last 6 months, and it started as a tool to solve a problem I always had as a game dev:

turn one character image into a full animated spritesheet quickly, while keeping the character consistent across the whole set.

  
The flow is pretty simple:

upload (or generate) a character image -> generate animations like idle / walk / run / attack / custom moves -> test it instantly in the browser -> export it into your game engine.

The part I care about most is bringing it all together into one simple workflow and speeding up creation time dramatically, without all the copy-pasting and hoping everything works.

  
In this new update/video I’m showing:

* custom character poses on demand
* state of the art background removal
* a brand new cutscene creator
* higher resolution exports
* faster generations

  
It now goes beyond just character animation now too, with support for props, items, VFX, cutscenes, large batch workflows, MCP, and API integrations. I’m also starting to explore the 3D side, which feels like a really exciting step toward a bigger and more complete game asset pipeline.

It’s not perfect and there’s lots of room to improve, but I’m trying to make it at least 1% better every day !

[https://www.autosprite.io/](https://www.autosprite.io/)

I’m excited to hear any feedback, Thank you!

replies.body: I've tried this path and while it creates videos of your concept image, they aren't very stable for sprite sheets.  I've moved to trying to take a concept image and use FLUX models to author small intentional movement frames.  But hey, I'm just a solo dev.  If there is a good way to make that work hit me up.

replies.author: story_of_the_beer
replies.body: What resolution size are you using? I've had much better luck using 720p, it retains pixel art well albeit doing a true pixel pass on the frames afterwards. My issue with qwen image edit (haven't really tried klein) is the produced image looks good but the results will be quite off frame which gives a uncanny vibe when tied together. Wan has it's rotoscope issue too but I feel it can be more manageable with prompting/seeds. Curious to know if klein works better for you.

replies.author: Isthan
replies.body:
I've tried 720 and 1024 as my target resolutions just for the purposes of generating frames.  The idea being that I could scale them down later (or not).  Its possible that this technique for generation could work, but when I tried doing some experiments the best frames I could isolate would produce a very jerky animation.  I think it could be good for idle positions where theres just chest/head movement.

  
Overall my current concept is to author specific frames by taking my concept image and using a prompt to do a very minor change in pose using flux klein.  I'll call a given prompt + source image a "corridor."  The idea is to "mine" a corridor until we can identify a good candidate, or move the prompt and create a new corridor to mine.  Then identify the best candidate frames and turn those into a sprite sheet.

  
Still a lot of fog for me in what is going to be practical and work, but thats my current direction.

replies.author: beelllllll
replies.body: AutoSprite uses a pipeline of different models based on the specific animation, the desired resolution, and whether the animation is looping or non-looping, and a lot of other factors. Also they are changing all the time as the latest and greatest come out.

comments.author: hugejew
comments.body:
hey! actual user subscriber - not a bot heh. I really appreciate this tool as I tried to do a bunch of this myself with Stable Diffusion locally and had unusable results. I tried using the standard fare tooling - Gemini, GPT, etc - and got nowhere either. I've gotten some very good animations from AutoSprite.

that said, there's a few things it could improve on:  
1. it doesn't handle quadrupeds well, especially with regard to nonstandard animations (climbing up onto something, celebrating, etc). I'd love to see the ability to specify quadruped.

2. asset animations - explosions, debris collapses, etc, don't seem to work very well. it would be great to see this fleshed out as much as the character animations are so that you can give it a start and an end, for example, or have it really follow full instructions.

3. the "bulk" option results seem disconnected from the single results in confusing ways. I don't always see the same animation sets for the same character in both places? it seems like they're a different animation set for some reason.

4. I'd love to be able to recover historical generations easily, or review them easily. sometimes I want to go back a few iterations and if I forgot to download that set, it seems gone, or if it's not gone, it's hidden in the UI.

overall though I think this is the best of the animation/sprite tools I've used. I actually have a hand-drawn asset so I can't speak to the full-on generation side, but from the handful of drawn pieces, I've been able to generate a lot of great animations to use in game. thanks!

replies.author: beelllllll
replies.body:
Thank you so much for the detailed feedback, this is super valuable.

For quadrupeds, **Humanoid** is on by default when creating a character. If you turn that off and add a short description, it should work much better. For existing characters, you can change that in the **Character** tab and save.

For explosions and similar effects, did you try the **Assets** tab instead of the **Character** tab? That flow supports first frame, last frame, and looping, and tends to work much better for those. I've gotten great explosion effects and animated props and such.

On bulk, yes, that part needs to be cleaner. Right now it does feel a bit separate. Sheets made in the advanced workflow do save on the normal app side too, but it usually works best to refresh the app side after you do a bulk animation.

Older generations are still saved too. On the preview or spritesheet tab, you can click through the version numbers. Sorry, that part is pretty small and easy to miss.

Also, have you tried **Ultra** or the new and improved default background removal in the last few weeks? I did a big overhaul there recently and it is much better now. I’ll definitely keep an eye on RMBG 3.0 too.

And thank you again, really appreciate you taking the time to write all this 🙏

replies.body:
nice - thanks for the reply. yeah I have humanoid off but often I've had the character stand up on hind legs or like, grow 2 more legs and be a 6-legged dogmonster.

I have used the assets tab yes - it works OK but there's some cases where I'd want to, say, have an explosion that billows up, then settles down into a debris pile, and it seems to only handle maybe 1-2s. perhaps an approach is to break it up and use the last frame to continue the animation manually. maybe some kind of feature like "continue animation" or "expand animation" might be interesting. consistency is key obv.

thanks for your work on this and your reply.
